title: Undo stack with instant minimum
prompt:
Implement a MinStack class whose push, pop, top and min methods each run in O(1) time, where min returns the smallest value currently on the stack.

- Fill in the class; the provided runMinStack / run_min_stack driver replays ops and is what the tests call.
- ops has 1 to 10,000 entries: ["push", x], ["pop"], ["top"] or ["min"], with x between -10^9 and 10^9.
- pop, top and min are only called when the stack is non-empty. pop removes the top value and returns nothing.
- The driver returns one entry per op: the value for top and min, null (None) for push and pop.
hints: Scanning the whole stack in min is O(n). What could you store at push time so the answer is already known?
Keep a second stack alongside the values: entry i holds the minimum of the first i + 1 values.
On push, store min(x, current min); on pop, pop both stacks. min just reads the top of the second stack.

solution.explanation: A parallel stack records, for every depth, the minimum of everything at or below that depth. Because a stack only changes at the top, popping restores the previous minimum automatically, so every method is O(1).

complexity.notes: The minimum stack can be made sparser by only pushing when x <= current minimum, but the worst case is still O(n).

followUps: Support max as well as min. Does the same trick work?
Build a queue with O(1) amortized min using two of these stacks.
